tools.name: backups_ingest
tools.description: Accepts a root JSON array of backup entries (v3 key). Each entry identifies a device, job, and client, and may include result collections for backups, replications, verifications, boot verifications, and alerts. The entire batch is rejected when any entry fails validation. The total number of results across all collections in a request must not exceed 10,000. A successful request is acknowledged with an empty `202 Accepted` response. Accepted results are queued for asynchronous processing by the backup results saver pipeline. Uses the ScalePad API key (BACKUP_RADAR_API_KEY).

tools.name: backups_retire
tools.description: Retires backups that match the supplied filters (v3 key). Filters are exact (case-insensitive) and combined with AND. `reason` is required. At least one filter is required. Set `dry_run` to `true` to preview every match without retiring anything. A live request retires every match and returns the full retired set. Tenant-level API keys are allowed. A user-tied key must belong to a tenant administrator or a user with the Retire Backup permission. Uses the ScalePad API key (BACKUP_RADAR_API_KEY). Required: reason. Optional: client_id, client_name, close_psa_tickets (default: false) (plus 5 more).

params.name: client_id
params.description: ScalePad Core client id. Matches only devices linked to that client. Unmapped devices are excluded.

params.name: client_name
params.description: Exact client name. Matches the ScalePad client name when the device is mapped; otherwise the Backup Radar company name. Matching is case-insensitive.

params.name: close_psa_tickets
params.description: When false, related tickets stay in Backup Radar only. When true, Backup Radar also attempts to close the ticket in the connected PSA.

params.name: device_id
params.description: ScalePad device id.

params.name: device_name
params.description: Exact device name. Matches the ScalePad device name when the device is mapped; otherwise the Backup Radar device name. Matching is case-insensitive.

params.name: dry_run
params.description: When true, return the match set and do not retire anything.

params.name: job_name
params.description: Exact backup job name. Matching is case-insensitive.

params.name: no_result_in
params.description: Retire backups with no result received in the last N days, including backups that have never received a result.

params.name: reason
params.description: Note stored on each retired backup and in the retire activity log.

tools.name: devices_list
tools.description: Returns a cursor-paginated list of backup devices whose names match the optional filters (v3 key). Each item includes the device's last result and per-day SLA history for the requested window, ending on the tenant's current local date. Devices are returned whether or not their Backup Radar company is mapped to a ScalePad company. When a device is not mapped, the ScalePad-specific fields (`device_id`, `device_name`, and the `client` `name`/`client_id`) are null. Uses the ScalePad API key (BACKUP_RADAR_API_KEY). Optional: page_size (default: 100), history_days, sort (plus 3 more).

params.name: page_size
params.description: Number of items per page. Must be between 1 and 200. Defaults to 100 when omitted.

params.name: history_days
params.description: Number of calendar days of backup history to return, ending on the tenant's current local date. Must be between 1 and 365.

params.name: sort
params.description: Sort order for a single field. **Syntax** - `field` or `+field`: ascending - `-field`: descending **Supported fields** - `device_name` - `device_id` **Examples** - `sort=device_name` - `sort=+device_name` - `sort=-device_name` - `sort=device_id` - `sort=-device_id`

params.name: cursor
params.description: The cursor from the previous response (`next_cursor`). Pass it here to fetch the next page.

params.name: device_name
params.description: Filter on device name using the operators below. Prefers the ScalePad `device_name` when the device is mapped; when it is not mapped to a ScalePad device, filters against `br_device_name` instead. **Operators:** `eq` (equality; this is the default) and `in` (match any value in the list). Use double quotes for values when the value contains a comma, a colon, or spaces. **Equality examples:** - `filter[device_name]=Server-01` - `filter[device_name]=eq:Server-01` - `filter[device_name]=eq:'Server, Primary'` - `filter[device_name]=eq:'Server: Primary'` **List examples:** - `filter[device_name]=in:Device-01,Device-02` - `filter[device_name]=in:Device-01,'Device, Primary'`

params.name: device_id
params.description: Filter on `device_id` (ScalePad device id) using the operators below. Devices that are not mapped to a ScalePad device are excluded when this filter is applied. **Operators:** `eq` (equality; this is the default) and `in` (match any value in the list). **Equality examples:** - `filter[device_id]=9999999b-6d54-44d7-b0b7-5600849ca5a4` - `filter[device_id]=eq:9999999b-6d54-44d7-b0b7-5600849ca5a4` **List examples:** - `filter[device_id]=in:9999999b-6d54-44d7-b0b7-5600849ca5a4,0aaaaaab-1111-2222-3333-444444444444`

Optional: page_size (default: 100), history_days, sort (plus 2 more).

params.name: page_size
params.description: Number of items per page. Must be between 1 and 200. Defaults to 100 when omitted.

params.name: history_days
params.description: Number of calendar days of backup health history to return, ending on the tenant's current local date. Must be between 1 and 365.

params.name: sort
params.description: Sort order for a single field. **Syntax** - `field` or `+field`: ascending - `-field`: descending **Supported field** - `client.name` **Examples** - `sort=client.name` - `sort=+client.name` - `sort=-client.name`

params.name: cursor
params.description: The cursor from the previous response (`next_cursor`). Pass it here to fetch the next page.

params.name: client_name
params.description: Filter on `client.name` using the operators below. **Operators:** `eq` (equality; this is the default) and `in` (match any value in the list). Use double quotes for values when the value contains a comma, a colon, or spaces. **Equality examples:** - `filter[client.name]=Corp` - `filter[client.name]=eq:Corp` - `filter[client.name]=eq:'Fabrik, LLC'` - `filter[client.name]=eq:'Solty: West'` **List examples:** - `filter[client.name]=in:Conto,Fabrik` - `filter[client.name]=in:Conto,'Fabrik, LLC'`

novel_features.name: Morning backup check
novel_features.description: One ranked list of today's failing, silent and at-risk backups, each marked new or ongoing with days in status and open ticket count; uses whichever keys you synced.

novel_features.name: Who is nobody watching
novel_features.description: Every backup Backup Radar receives but nobody acts on: inactive, unmapped to ScalePad, failing with no ticket, no PSA company, or warnings counted as success by policy. Unmapped needs the v3 key; the other reasons need the v2 key.

novel_features.name: Cross-vendor coverage diff
novel_features.description: Compare the devices a backup vendor protects against what Backup Radar monitors and list the gaps in both directions.

novel_features.name: Retire candidates
novel_features.description: Backups with no result in N days, grouped by client, with retire request bodies ready to preview; works from either key's synced data.

novel_features.name: Client compliance scorecard
novel_features.description: In-compliance rate, weekly trend and worst devices for one client, or every client ranked, from up to a year of client health (v3 key); worst devices use synced device history (each sync fetches 90 days; stored days accumulate up to a year).

novel_features.name: Device timeline
novel_features.description: One device's day-by-day backup story merged from both API generations, with tickets, tags and notes; --live adds each day's v2 results (v2 key).

novel_features.name: Validated bulk ingest
novel_features.description: Push flat CSV or JSONL backup results into Backup Radar (v3 key, live write) with local validation and automatic batching under the 10,000-result limit.
